The Robot Tells

12 giveaways that prove AI wrote your content, and a 30-second fix for each

People don't need a detector to spot AI writing. They just feel it. The post is smooth, polite, and weirdly empty, so they scroll past.

This checklist shows you the 12 patterns that give it away. Each one has a fast fix and a before/after so you can see it work. Run your next draft through it before you hit post. It takes about two minutes.

01 The throat-clearing opener

How to spot it: The first line talks about the world instead of the point. "In today's fast-paced digital landscape..."

30-second fix: Delete the first sentence. Start with the thing you actually wanted to say.

BeforeIn today's fast-paced digital world, building an audience is more important than ever.
AfterNobody followed me for the first 90 days.

02 "It's not X, it's Y"

How to spot it: A claim set up as a fake contrast. "It's not about posting more. It's about posting better." AI loves this shape.

30-second fix: Say the claim once, plainly, and back it with one fact.

BeforeIt's not about working harder. It's about working smarter.
AfterI cut my posts from 7 a week to 3 and got more replies.

03 The perfect triplet

How to spot it: Every list has exactly three tidy items. "Clear, concise, and compelling."

30-second fix: Keep only the item that is actually true. Or use two. Or use four. Break the pattern.

BeforeGreat copy is clear, concise, and compelling.
AfterGreat copy is clear. That's the whole job.

04 The vocabulary tell

How to spot it: Words real people almost never say out loud: delve, tapestry, leverage, unlock, elevate, game-changer, seamless, robust, navigate the landscape.

30-second fix: Say it the way you'd say it to a friend across the table. Swap each fancy word for the plain one.

BeforeLet's delve into how you can leverage this game-changing tool.
AfterHere's how to use this tool.

05 Em dash overload

How to spot it: Dashes everywhere, holding sentences together that should have been two sentences.

30-second fix: Allow yourself one per post at most. Everywhere else, use a period.

BeforeThe offer is simple, it's fast, and it works, even if you're starting from zero.
AfterThe offer is simple. It's fast. It works even if you're starting from zero.

06 Fake hype

How to spot it: Cheerful filler: "Let's dive in!" "Buckle up!" "Here's the thing." Energy with no information.

30-second fix: Cut every line that announces what you're about to say. Just say it.

BeforeBuckle up, because we're about to dive into something amazing!
AfterHere's the exact DM I sent.

07 Vague claims

How to spot it: "Many people struggle with..." "Studies show..." No number, no name, no price, no date.

30-second fix: Add one concrete detail: a number, a name, a place, a price, or a day of the week.

BeforeMany beginners struggle to make their first sale.
AfterMost beginners I talk to are 60 days in with $0 and 4 half-built products.

08 Perfect rhythm

How to spot it: Every paragraph is the same length. Every sentence is the same shape. It reads like a metronome.

30-second fix: Break it up. Add a one-line paragraph. Use a fragment. Let one sentence run long and the next stop short.

BeforePosting daily builds trust. Trust leads to sales. Sales create growth.
AfterPost daily. Trust comes first. Sales come after, sometimes a lot after.

09 The summary closer

How to spot it: "In conclusion..." "Ultimately..." "At the end of the day..." The post repeats itself to feel finished.

30-second fix: End on your last useful point, or on a question you actually want answered.

BeforeIn conclusion, consistency and authenticity are key to long-term success.
AfterWhat's the one post you've been avoiding?

10 Hedging mush

How to spot it: "It's important to note that..." "This can potentially help..." "May improve..." Nothing is ever committed to.

30-second fix: Say it or cut it. If you're not sure, say that you're not sure, and say why.

BeforeIt's important to note that this approach can potentially help improve results.
AfterThis worked for me. I don't know if it'll work for you.

11 Emoji bullet lists

How to spot it: Every point has a rocket, a checkmark, or a lightbulb, with a bold header, even for a three-line post.

30-second fix: Write sentences. Use at most one emoji, or none.

Before🚀 Boost engagement
✅ Save time
💡 Grow faster
AfterThis saves me about an hour a day, and my replies went up.

12 No scars, no opinion

How to spot it: Nothing in the post could only have come from you. No story, no mistake, no opinion that someone might disagree with.

30-second fix: Add one thing that happened to you, with a detail only you would know. Then take a side.

BeforeEmail marketing is a powerful tool for any business.
AfterMy first email list was 14 people, and 6 were family. I still sent every email like it mattered.

The 2-minute pass before you post

  1. Read the first line out loud. If it talks about "the world" or "today's landscape", delete it.
  2. Search the draft for dashes and fancy words (delve, leverage, unlock, elevate, seamless). Replace them.
  3. Find every vague claim and add one real number, name, or detail.
  4. Make one paragraph shorter than the others. Make one longer.
  5. Cut the last paragraph if it just repeats the post.
  6. Add one sentence only you could have written.

Score your draft

Count how many of the 12 tells you find. 0 to 2 reads like a person. 3 to 5 reads like a person using AI, which is fine if the story is yours. 6 or more reads like a robot, and readers will keep scrolling.

The goal is not to hide that you used AI. The goal is to make something worth reading. Fix these 12 and your posts will sound like you again.
